about: Contextual person and community register. Short descriptions are editorial summaries of the cited sources and the Sīrah chapters; they are neither full biographies nor proofs of every attribution. Sources remain subject to textual verification.

groups.name: Earlier prophets and primordial figures
groups.intro: The formative prophetic histories that establish the original vocation

groups.name: The prophetic household and kin
groups.intro: Those through whom domestic life, protection and family relationships become intelligible

groups.name: First believers and emigrants
groups.intro: Those whose actions carry early instruction, migration, confession and community formation

groups.name: Madinan groups, allies and opponents
groups.intro: The social world of Yathrib and Makkah, including major clans, opponents and negotiations

groups.name: Wider world and later inheritors
groups.intro: Rulers, scholars, patrons and historical actors through whom forms of guidance entered diverse societies

entries.name: Ādam
entries.role: First human and recipient of the Names
entries.bio: Receives the divine teaching of the names and the earthly vocation of khilāfa. The Garden, the lapse and repentance frame the human need for revealed guidance.

entries.name: Ādam’s spouse (Ḥawwāʾ)
entries.bio: Shares the Garden's prohibition, temptation and acknowledgement of wrongdoing with Ādam. The Qurʾān identifies her as his spouse; the name Ḥawwāʾ comes from later tradition.

entries.name: Iblīs
entries.bio: Refuses the command to bow to Ādam, appealing to fire and clay. His self-justification and temptation provide a recurring case of restricted vision and misdirected will.

entries.name: Nūḥ
entries.bio: Calls his people to worship God, builds the Ark under revelation and seeks guidance concerning his son when the flood comes.

entries.name: Hūd
entries.bio: Challenges the arrogance of a people who possess strength, architecture and power, calling them to worship God and repent.

entries.name: Ṣāliḥ
entries.bio: Presents the she-camel as a sign demanding respect for the creature's appointed share of water and the divine command.

entries.name: Lūṭ
entries.bio: Strives to protect guests from an approaching crowd and receives divine deliverance amid the corruption of his people.

entries.name: Shuʿayb
entries.bio: Calls people to worship God and to keep proper measures and honest commercial dealings.

entries.name: Ibrāhīm
entries.role: Prophetic patriarch and builder of the House
entries.bio: His covenant, family and sanctuary connect worship to settlement, prayer, security and provision. He and Ismāʿīl raise the House's foundations.

entries.name: Ismāʿīl
entries.bio: Assists Ibrāhīm at the House and is singled out for truthfulness to his promise and instruction of his household in prayer and giving.

entries.name: Isḥāq
entries.role: Son of Ibrāhīm and a prophet
entries.bio: Remembered in the Qurʾānic family of prophetic guidance, alongside his son Yaʿqūb.

entries.name: Yaʿqūb
entries.bio: His household's separation, trial and reunion provide the familial setting for Yūsuf's story.

entries.name: Yūsuf
entries.bio: Interprets dreams, withstands trial and eventually oversees provision during years of scarcity in Egypt.

entries.name: Mūsā
entries.bio: Confronts Pharaoh, guides the Israelites and receives revelation governing worship and community. In the Miʿrāj reports he counsels Muḥammad concerning the community's capacity for prayer.

entries.name: al-Khiḍr
entries.role: Guide in the journey of Mūsā
entries.bio: The figure accompanying Mūsā in Qurʾān 18:60–82. The narrative explores the relation of visible events, concealed grounds and extraordinary disclosure.

entries.name: Dāwūd
entries.bio: Combines praise, skilled workmanship and judgment within prophetic kingship.

entries.name: Sulaymān
entries.bio: Receives wide dominion and knowledge while exercising political judgment, including the encounter with the ruler of Sheba.

entries.name: Ayyūb
entries.bio: Responds to suffering through supplication and receives divine guidance concerning a bodily means of relief.

entries.name: Yūnus
entries.bio: His departure, supplication in darkness and the repentance of his people illustrate the return to divine mercy.

entries.name: Zakariyyā
entries.bio: Prays for a worthy successor while recognizing the child's arrival as a gift from God.

entries.name: Yaḥyā
entries.bio: Receives wisdom and is remembered for piety and tender regard for his parents.

entries.name: Maryam
entries.bio: Her trust and dependence upon God encompass extraordinary provision and ordinary embodied effort.

entries.name: ʿĪsā
entries.bio: His extraordinary signs of healing and life are described as occurring by God's permission and call people to worship God.

entries.name: Queen of Sheba
entries.bio: Her exchange with Sulaymān involves diplomacy, examination of signs and a decisive response to his summons. Her personal name occurs in later tradition.

entries.name: Muḥammad ﷺ
entries.role: Final Messenger and central figure of the Sīrah
entries.bio: Receives the Qurʾān, teaches worship, forms companions and addresses the rights and circumstances of persons through his words, actions and judgments.

entries.name: Khadījah
entries.bio: Receives the Prophet after the first revelation, remembers the pattern of his character and sustains the earliest household of believers.

entries.name: ʿĀʾishah
entries.bio: Transmits reports about worship and household life, corrects misunderstandings and instructs later students.

entries.name: Fāṭimah
entries.bio: Member of the Prophet's household, wife of ʿAlī and mother of al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn. Her descendants and standing became important in later debates over authority.

entries.name: ʿAlī
entries.role: Cousin, son-in-law and fourth caliph in Sunni sequence
entries.bio: Close member of the Prophet's household, husband of Fāṭimah and father of al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn. His caliphate confronted conflict over succession and retaliation.

entries.name: al-Ḥasan
entries.bio: Son of ʿAlī and Fāṭimah; his political settlement with Muʿāwiyah is important to the history of leadership after the first civil war.

entries.name: al-Ḥusayn
entries.role: Grandson of the Prophet and figure of Karbalāʾ
entries.bio: Son of ʿAlī and Fāṭimah. He and companions were killed at Karbalāʾ in 680, an event central to subsequent Muslim historical memory.

entries.name: Abū Ṭālib
entries.bio: Provided kin-based protection to the Prophet in Makkah. His death affected the Prophet's security during the Meccan mission.

entries.name: Ḥamzah
entries.role: Uncle of the Prophet and companion
entries.bio: A prominent supporter of the early Muslim community, killed at the Battle of Uḥud.

entries.name: Umm Salamah
entries.bio: At al-Ḥudaybiyyah she advised the Prophet to perform the rites visibly when the companions were distressed and slow to respond.

entries.name: Banū Hāshim
entries.bio: The clan within Quraysh to which Muḥammad belonged. Its kin ties affected protection, economic pressure and the politics of early allegiance.

entries.name: Abū Bakr
entries.role: Early companion and first caliph in Sunni sequence
entries.bio: Companion in the Hijrah and later a central participant in the succession debates and the consolidation of public obligations after 632.

entries.name: ʿUmar
entries.bio: Asked the Prophet about dedicating valuable property at Khaybar, a formative endowment precedent. Later ruled amid major conquests and administrative changes.

entries.name: ʿUthmān
entries.bio: Led the expanding community after ʿUmar. Disputes concerning his administration preceded his killing in 656.

entries.name: Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr
entries.bio: Taught Qurʾānic recitation and prayer in Yathrib before the Hijrah, helping form local believers prepared to welcome the Prophet.

entries.name: Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib
entries.bio: A relative of the Prophet who is remembered as explaining the Muslim faith at the Negus's court during the early migration.

entries.name: Bilāl
entries.bio: Formerly enslaved companion remembered for his devotion and association with the public call to prayer.

entries.name: Abū Jandal
entries.role: Vulnerable believer at the Hudaybiyyah negotiations
entries.bio: A son of the Meccan negotiator Suhayl ibn ʿAmr, whose arrival seeking protection made the treaty's controversial return clause immediate and painful.

entries.name: Māʿiz
entries.role: Penitent in a transmitted judicial encounter
entries.bio: Presented a confession of adultery to the Prophet. The report includes repeated questioning, public judgment and later discussion of repentance.

entries.name: Woman of Ghāmid
entries.role: Penitent mother in a judicial encounter
entries.bio: Sought judgment concerning adultery; pregnancy and care of her child shaped the course of the case. The transmitted narrative also concerns repentance and public speech.

entries.name: Muhājirūn
entries.bio: Those who left Makkah for refuge or the new Medinan community. Their loss of property and protection created obligations of hospitality and mutual aid.

entries.name: Anṣār
entries.bio: The believers of Yathrib who welcomed the Prophet and emigrants, undertaking hospitality, teaching and common defence.

entries.name: Aws
entries.role: One of the major groups of Yathrib
entries.bio: A major tribal grouping in Yathrib alongside Khazraj, with its own alliances and earlier conflicts. Members later participated in the Medinan community.

entries.name: Khazraj
entries.role: One of the major groups of Yathrib
entries.bio: A principal Medinan grouping alongside Aws, whose members were among those engaged in the earliest pledges and formation of the Anṣār.

entries.name: Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī
entries.bio: Among the Anṣār remembered for hosting the Prophet after his arrival in Madinah.

entries.name: Anas ibn Mālik
entries.bio: Served the Prophet for years and later transmitted memories of his daily conduct, including patient attention toward those serving him.

entries.name: Saʿd ibn Muʿādh
entries.bio: An important Medinan figure whose leadership and relations to Banū Qurayẓa appear in reports of the Trench's aftermath.

entries.name: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy
entries.bio: A local leader whose relationship to the Prophet's community features in accounts of divided loyalties at Madinah.
entries.source: Sīrah chapter 15 and reports of Medina

entries.name: Quraysh
entries.bio: The principal Meccan community around the Kaʿbah, including those who protected the Prophet and those who opposed his mission. Its leaders negotiated the Hudaybiyyah truce.

entries.name: Banū Qaynuqāʿ
entries.bio: One of the groups named in traditional accounts of the Jewish communities of Medina; particular treaties and conflicts require comparison across recensions.

entries.name: Banū Naḍīr
entries.bio: A named Jewish community in the transmitted Medinan narratives. Its relations with the new public order and later conflict require source-critical analysis.

entries.name: Banū Qurayẓa
entries.bio: Appears in the accounts of alliances and the siege of Madinah; the reported aftermath and judicial details have an extensive and debated historiography.

entries.name: Abū Jahl
entries.bio: Meccan leader remembered for opposition to the early Muslims; killed at the Battle of Badr.

entries.name: Abū Sufyān
entries.role: Meccan leader and later member of Muslim community
entries.bio: An influential figure in Quraysh's conflicts with the early Muslims and the political changes around the conquest of Makkah.

entries.name: Suhayl ibn ʿAmr
entries.bio: Represented Quraysh in the treaty negotiations. His son Abū Jandal arrived during the agreement, making a clause concerning fugitives immediately contentious.

entries.name: Hind bint ʿUtbah
entries.role: Meccan figure connected to Quraysh leadership
entries.bio: A prominent Meccan woman in accounts of the conflicts with the early Muslim community and later changes at Makkah.

entries.name: Aṣḥamah (the Negus)
entries.role: Ruler of Aksum and protector of emigrants
entries.bio: The ruler who provided refuge to early Muslim emigrants. The Prophet later announced his death and prayed for him, according to hadith reports.

entries.name: Heraclius
entries.bio: Ruled the Eastern Roman Empire during the emergence of the Prophet's mission; the wider imperial conflicts formed part of Arabia's political setting.

entries.name: Khusraw II
entries.bio: Sasanian ruler of Iran during its long conflict with the Eastern Roman Empire in the decades surrounding the mission.

entries.name: Muʿāwiyah
entries.bio: Opposed ʿAlī during the first civil war and subsequently ruled from Damascus. The transition to dynastic succession became a major political question.

entries.name: Yazīd
entries.bio: Succeeded his father Muʿāwiyah; the killing of al-Ḥusayn at Karbalāʾ occurred during his rule.

entries.name: Abū Muslim
entries.bio: Led forces central to the Abbasid revolution in Khurāsān and the defeat of Umayyad power in 750.

entries.name: al-Manṣūr
entries.bio: Founded Baghdad as a new imperial capital in 762, a city that later supported major communities of learning.

entries.name: al-Maʾmūn
entries.bio: Associated with scholarly patronage and with the *miḥnah*, the state-backed testing of a disputed theological proposition.

entries.name: Hārūn al-Rashīd
entries.bio: His court and its networks of patronage belong to the scholarly and administrative history of Baghdad.

entries.name: Ḥunayn ibn Isḥāq
entries.bio: Known for comparing copies of Greek medical texts and preparing Syriac and Arabic translations for patrons and practitioners.

entries.name: Abū Ḥanīfah
entries.bio: A major figure associated with the formation of the Ḥanafī legal tradition through the work of his students.

entries.name: Mālik ibn Anas
entries.bio: Associated with the *Muwaṭṭaʾ* and the scholarly life of Madinah; his students transmitted varying recensions and later interpretations.

entries.name: al-Shāfiʿī
entries.bio: A leading contributor to the articulation of juristic evidence and legal method, especially in the tradition of *al-Risāla*.

entries.name: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal
entries.bio: Important to the collection and evaluation of prophetic reports and the later formation of Ḥanbalī legal thought.

entries.name: al-Ghazālī
entries.bio: Explored the validity of outward acts, intellectual argument, character formation and the inward meanings of worship.

entries.name: Ibn Rushd
entries.bio: Produced influential analyses of juristic disagreement and philosophical demonstration in al-Andalus.

entries.name: Ibn ʿArabī
entries.bio: Developed major accounts of prophetic wisdom, divine manifestation and spiritual realization, subsequently elaborated by students and commentators.

entries.name: al-Qūnawī
entries.bio: A major successor in the intellectual tradition of Ibn ʿArabī, associated with technical accounts of spiritual knowledge and the comprehensive station.

entries.name: al-Farghānī
entries.bio: Explained the correspondence of divine disclosure, the Qurʾān and embodied prophetic perfection through a developed metaphysical vocabulary.

entries.name: Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn
entries.bio: United political and military resources for campaigns in Syria and Palestine and the recovery of Jerusalem in 1187.

entries.name: Nūr al-Dīn
entries.bio: Associated with the earlier political consolidation and public patronage that preceded Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn's campaigns.

entries.name: Ghāzān
entries.bio: His public conversion to Islam in 1295 became important to Ilkhanid religious policy; local religious practices changed unevenly.

entries.name: Aḥmad Tegüder
entries.bio: An Ilkhanid ruler who professed Islam before Ghāzān; his case corrects simple dynastic conversion chronologies.

entries.name: Mansa Mūsā
entries.bio: His pilgrimage in 1324 publicized Mali's wealth and its connections with wider Muslim regions.

entries.name: Aḥmad Bābā
entries.bio: Known for learned works and for displacement following Moroccan intervention in the Songhay world.

entries.name: Khān Jahān
entries.bio: Remembered in accounts of settlement and infrastructure around Bagerhat. His dated tomb inscription provides an important historical anchor.

entries.name: Akbar
entries.bio: His court pursued debates and policies of imperial inclusion amid religious plurality in India.

entries.name: Aurangzeb
entries.bio: Patronized a substantial Ḥanafī legal compilation through a group of jurists while governing an empire with varied local institutions.

entries.name: Dārā Shukoh
entries.role: Mughal prince and comparative religious author
entries.bio: Sponsored a Persian rendering of Sanskrit Upaniṣadic texts and interpreted them through his own contested universalizing framework.

entries.name: Shāh Walī Allāh
entries.bio: Developed work on hadith, juristic reasoning and spiritual thought within the conditions of late Mughal India.
